data.name: All the Delicate Duplicates
data.detailed_description:
All The Delicate Duplicates is a short, experimental single player first-person narrative game.

Story


John, a computer engineer and single father, inherits a collection of arcane objects from Mo, his mysterious relative. Over time, John and his daughter Charlotte begin to realise that these objects have unusual physical properties – and that the more they are exposed to them, the more their reality and memories appear to change.

Features

  • Part game part reading experience with multiple interpretations.
  • Non-linear narrative that pieces together through interactive discoveries in the game world and a text-based backstory.
  • Surreal domestic environments spread across different timelines with open exploration.
  • Mezangelle: a poetic language created by Mez Breeze that stacks layers of meanings into single phrases.

Warnings

All The Delicate Duplicates contains minimal strobe-like effects, minimal to moderate profanity, potentially creepy psychological concepts and themes.

reviews.review:
If you're expecting a story rich game, do not buy this.

Gameplay consist solely of just walking around and picking up items to look at them.

It feels like project from a student thrown together in a few weekends with the intent to try and make the game deep or something, it feels more like /r/Im14AndThisIsDeep because it contains more or less nothing. It is just trying to use already existing tropes here and there to make you think "omg... wow.... this is so deep" when in fact it is not, it is nonsensical garbage made up and it doesn't mean anything, with dumb graphical effects to make you feel as if it is such a trippy and 'woah' game.

Think Dear Esther, which is made by students just huffing their own farts but at least they [i]tried[/i] to achieve something, but without any story at all and instead occasionally some trope happens, you can just imagine the students faces: https://i.imgur.com/gSa3rdX.png - "They just don't get it" while huffing their own farts. 

The positive reviews are almost giving me 2nd-hand embarrassment. People are acting as if this is some amazing "WOW" game and being blown away by simple, garbage 'psychedelic' effects.
Any person that is fully developed and self-aware cannot play something like this and see it as some amazing wow-factor philosophically deep game, it isn't at all.

The game is laden with motion blur, over-exaggerated blooming and other garbage effects.

Even if it was completely different and was half-decent, 8$ for a copy-pasted asset game is ridiculous.

No options menu, like, literally no options or settings menu exists. 
Weird to not have controller support in a game like this, it would be incredibly easy to add. The 'Partial Controller Support' tag is a lie.

[i]If you liked this review or otherwise found it helpful in deciding whether or not to buy this game, feel free to follow [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/29162366/]my Curator page[/url].[/i]
